title: Alignment-induced waste & page-compaction simulation — notes
content:
Summary:

Observed a class of OOMs that correlate poorly with total resident usage reported by nvidia-smi but correlate strongly with allocation failure patterns in logs. Hypothesis: alignment and page-granularity placement inside our slab/mempool allocator causes internal fragmentation that prevents reuse co-location; under certain allocation size mixes the allocator leaves small unusable gaps that cannot be satisfied by cudamalloc/cudamallocAsync fallback paths.

This doc captures experiments, a lightweight simulator we ran to quantify alignment waste, telemetry queries to find likely customers/clusters, and short-term mitigations to reduce the outage surface. The goal is to offer reproducible steps and concrete, low-risk mitigations we can push in the next minor runtime release.

Key observations from field incidents:
- OOM manifests as a sudden cudaMalloc retry loop with repeated "out of memory" from the driver, even though overall free memory reported by nvml was ~5-8% when sampled.
- Allocation trace heatmaps show many small allocations (1–8 MiB) sprinkled between a few very large KV cache blocks. The small allocations are high-frequency and short-lived (tens to hundreds of ms).
- When we forced best-effort compaction by proactively freeing and re-reserving large workspace slabs we could often restore throughput; suggests fragmentation rather than leak.
- Some customers on Ampere+ hardware show worse behavior because of larger page sizes and alignment of device allocations (CUDA 12 drivers aligning more aggressively).

Repro approach (local lab):
1) Start runtime with mempool enabled and detailed alloc logging (ALLOC_TRACE=1).
2) Use synthetic workload generator: mix of large KV writes (200-600 MiB, long-lived) + micro-requests pattern that alloc 512 KiB-8 MiB temporaries with 10–50 ms lifetime.
3) Run at 70–85% target utilization and observe failure spectrum.
4) Experiment with different slab/slot alignment (16B, 4 KiB, 2 MiB) and different arena sizes.

Simulator (toy model we used):
- Implemented in ~500 lines of Python (attached in repo link) — models a single GPU address space with page grain (default 65,536 bytes for CUDA internal GC on some drivers) and allocation/free events.
- Inputs: per-size histogram, alignment rules, slab split/coalescence policy, deferred-free latency distribution (simulating CUDA async frees).
- Outputs: time-series of free-span size distribution, count of unusable fragments, predicted probability of allocation failure for given request size.

Simulator results (selected):
- When alignment rounded allocations up to nearest 64 KiB, effective usable memory drops by 8–12% for workloads with >40% small allocations.
- Deferred-free latency >50 ms causes the unusable-fragment set to accumulate; combined with large long-lived KV blocks this produces a >99th-percentile allocation failure within 30–90 s under stress.
- Enabling coalescing on free boundaries in the simulator reduced failure risk by ~40%, but only when coalescing could be guaranteed to run frequently (sub-100 ms).

Telemetry queries used to identify real clusters with this mix: (pseudo-SQL / bigquery-ish)
- sample: SELECT cluster_id, gpu_model, frac_small_allocs, avg_alloc_latency_ms, pct_95_alloc_time FROM runtime.alloc_histograms WHERE window = last_24h ORDER BY frac_small_allocs DESC LIMIT 200
- Pattern to flag: frac_small_allocs > 0.35 AND avg_alloc_latency_ms > 12 AND pct_95_alloc_time > 80
- Found ~9 clusters in prod (past 3 months) matching pattern; 5 of them had incident tickets that overlapped with our alert windows.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Alignment rounding up to large page granularity (driver / CUDA behavior) multiplies waste when small allocations are frequent.
2) Our mempool slab splitting strategy favors fast allocation but fragments arenas because splits aren't re-coalesced quickly enough.
3) Deferred frees coming from CUDA stream synchronization delay returning memory into global free lists, exacerbating fragmentation at high concurrency.
4) Host pinned + UVM allocations increase compaction complexity because they lock certain pages into pinned regions.

Quick mitigations (low-risk):
- Tune runtime to avoid splitting slabs below a configurable threshold for tenant pools with observed high small-allocation fraction. This reduces micro-fragmentation at cost of some internal waste for small pools. (Proto patch: change split-min to 8 KiB in arena config)
- Decrease default deferred-free grace to 16 ms for high-throughput pools (we already have telemetry-driven knob per-pool). Risk: may increase contention on free-list locks; need perf regression tests.
- Add a telemetry flag that surfaces "alignment-waste ratio" per host (estimate from allocation trace) so SRE can triage at cluster level.

Medium-term mitigations (higher effort):
- Implement periodic compaction thread that runs at low-priority and attempts to coalesce free spans across slabs (job similar to jemalloc background thread). The challenge: must avoid long device stalls and coordinate with CUDA stream lifetimes.
- Introduce a small-object allocator (fixed-size bins) to handle 512 KiB and smaller allocations; reduces variance and internal fragmentation for micro-allocs.
- Explore kernel/driver flags or CUDA runtime parameters to reduce alignment rounding — may be vendor/driver dependent and not portable.

Experiments we ran and logs: (summary)
- Experiment A: flip split-min from 1 KiB -> 8 KiB -> 64 KiB on a 48 GiB GPU with synthetic stress. Result: 8 KiB point reduced failure rate by 60%, 64 KiB reduced throughput by 7% but eliminated failures.
- Experiment B: background coalescer running every 50 ms (heuristic) reduced unusable-fragment count by 35% but induced ~2–3 ms P99 latency blips on some request types.
- Experiment C: enable eager host->device prefetch for some KV writes; mixed results — reduced short-lived device allocations but increased pinned memory pressure.

Telemetry to add (recommended):
- Per-pool: allocation size histogram with alignment-adjusted bucket; deferred-free latency distribution; free-span histogram by size class.
- Per-node: estimated alignment-waste percent (how much memory is unusable due to rounding).
- Incident tags: correlate OOM events with recent large KV writes and new model deployments (sometimes model size increases push edge-case allocations over threshold).

Open questions / unknowns:
- What exact alignment policy is used by newer CUDA drivers on each GPU generation (Ampere vs Hopper)? Need to confirm with vendor docs or microbenchmarks.
- Is there a cheap way to force driver-level compaction/coalesce via CUDA APIs without driver restart?
- Are there workloads that rely on the current fast-split behavior for latency-sensitive short requests and would regress if we increased split-min? Need per-tenant A/B.

Action items (next 30 days):
- [Priya] finalize and land split-min tuning patch behind feature flag (INF-3201). Add unit tests for allocation correctness.
- [Liam] add telemetry estimates for alignment-waste and deferred-free percentiles; hook into existing alerting dashboard.
- [Sofia] run extended perf tests (48h) with split-min=8 KiB across 6 model-serving stacks and collect P95/P99 latencies.
- [Noah] instrument background coalescer prototype and measure tail-latency side effects.

Notes to self / stray ideas:
- Consider OS-level NUMA-affinity for host-pinned allocations to reduce fragmentation interactions when multiple processes share the GPU.
- Could we exploit CUDA MPS partitioning to isolate long-lived KV pools from short-lived micro-alloc workload? Adds operational complexity.

References / useful commands:
- nvprof / Nsight metrics for allocation stalls (custom traces).
- example debug query: grep ALLOC_TRACE runtime.log | sed -n '1,500p' | awk '{print $5, $8}' to collapse size and outcome.
- Simulator repo: github.com/redwood-repo/infra-tools/alloc-sim (private) — includes scenario configs used above.

Conclusion:
This is a promising lead: alignment-induced internal fragmentation + slow deferred freeing explains many of the observed symptom clusters. Short-term tuning (split-min, deferred-free knob) gives measurable benefit with limited risk and should be our first patch. Medium-term, a hybrid approach (small-object allocator + optional coalescer) looks necessary for robust behavior at scale.

TODO: attach simulation CSVs and raw alloc traces to INF-3124 ticket before proposing rollout plan.

-- Priya
